name: Railroad Crossing Advance Warning
spec: yellow circle with a large black X and the letters R R in two quadrants
meaning: A railroad crossing is ahead; slow down, look and listen.

snippets.back: People walking or bicycling near the road, animals, railroad crossings, intersections, bridges, curves and steep descents call for extra caution.
Red flashing lights work with crossbuck signs at many railroad crossings, and you must always stop when they begin flashing because a train is near, checking every track before you cross.
A motorcyclist approaching railroad tracks may slow down, rise off the seat or change angle to cross the tracks more directly.
The railroad regulatory sign means approach with caution and make sure every track is clear before you cross.
At a railroad gate or flagger's stop signal, remain stopped until the gate rises or the flagger ends the stop signal.
A railroad-crossing-ahead warning sign means slow down, look carefully both ways and be ready to stop, since a train cannot stop quickly.
Do not pass within one hundred feet before an intersection or railroad crossing or while crossing either one.
Slow down near street, highway and railroad crossings, near flags, flares or fuses on the road, and approaching hill crests and curves.

evidence: [sec08-card-sec08-F44 | AL p.49] A railroad-crossing-ahead warning sign means slow down, look carefully both ways and be ready to stop, since a train cannot stop quickly.
result.summary: Official snippet confirms advance warning meaning to slow down and look both ways; no snippet describes yellow circle/X/RR shape.
